scenario: AITA for wanting my girlfriend to be less braggy about her work perks? She seems to forget that the way she lives isn't how most people live... | My girlfriend has a pretty sweet job. She doesn't have set hours; she just has to work 35 hours a week whenever is convenient for her and make it to her few meetings. She can work from the office or from home sometimes. She has a full benefits package despite being under what most people consider full time. A really nice retirement package too. And the company will pay everything for continued education. She does work she finds interesting (cutting edge robotics) and gets along well with her coworkers. She has a lot of PTO per year and her boss even lets the employees "earn up" more; if they work extra hours one week they can ask for the equivalent in PTO for later. Her team's managers buy them whatever they want for the office; they want a 500 dollar expresso maker, they get it. They want a type of fancy coffee, they get it. Nice furniture, done... They get paid well too; pretty middle of the road salary for robotics but she says the work life balance more than makes up for it. She'd rather have more time than be a top earner. And honestly a midrange robotics salary is still damn good. And anyway, For a while I thought "good for her" for having found something that she is happy with. But recently it's gotten frustrating because I think she forgets that this isn't how everyone lives. Like when we're out with my friends or just hanging out she'll talk about the nice stuff her managers bought for the office, about all the vacations she takes, about how she and her coworkers left the office in the middle of the day to see a movie then came back and just worked a little later. And yeah, it seems like she forgets that is no way a normal job. So last night we were at a party and she mentioned how she was going to tour a few new apartments Monday morning and afternoon, and one of the people at the party was like "don't you have work" and she said "yeah but I can set my own hours" And that just rubbed me the wrong way and I said that she needed to stop going on and on about her work perks, it was obnoxious and came off braggy. She was like "I was just explaining something" and I said it wasn't just this, it was everything. Most people don't live the life she lives." She said that I was coming off jealous and that it was a bad look. That she was where she was because she didn't settle for less; she studied and worked her ass off, and didn't let herself get too settled anywhere she was unfulfilled. And that instead of complaining, maybe I should ask myself what I'm feeling jealous of and what I need to do to get it. I told her she was missing the point; she'll always be around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a little more modest about it. She said I was the only one who seemed to have a problem with it, and stormed off... AITA for what I said?

First, my girlfriend has a really great job. She works in robotics, which is a cool field. Her job offers a lot of flexibilityâĢĶshe can set her own hours, work from home sometimes, and has a good benefits package. She also gets paid well, and her company even pays for continued education. Plus, she has a lot of PTO (paid time off) and her bosses are really generous with office perks like expensive coffee machines and nice furniture. It sounds like she's really happy with her job and the work-life balance it provides. At first, I was happy for her. I thought it was awesome that she found a job she's happy with. But lately, it's been getting frustrating. She talks a lot about her job perks, especially when we're out with friends or just hanging out. For example, she mentioned that she was going to tour some apartments on Monday morning and afternoon, and someone asked if she had work. She replied that she could set her own hours, which kind of rubbed me the wrong way. I told her she needed to stop bragging about her work perks because it was obnoxious. She defended herself by saying she was just explaining something and that I was being jealous. She pointed out that she worked hard to get where she is and that she didn't settle for less. She suggested I should figure out what I'm feeling jealous of and work on that instead of complaining. I tried to explain that she's always around people who don't have what she does, and she could be a bit more modest. She said I was the only one with a problem and stormed off. Now, I'm wondering if I'm the asshole here. Let me think about this. On one hand, her job is amazing, and she's lucky to have it. She's worked hard for it, and it's understandable that she's proud. However, when she talks about her job perks in social settings, it might come off as bragging, especially if others around her don't have similar opportunities. I can see how that might make people feel uncomfortable or jealous, especially if they're struggling with their own jobs or financial situations. On the other hand, she's just sharing her experiences and being honest about her job. She might not realize that others perceive her comments as bragging. She could be unaware of how her words affect others, especially if she's not intentionally trying to boast. I also need to consider my own feelings. Am I jealous of her job? Do I feel like I'm not as successful or that I'm missing out on similar opportunities? If that's the case, maybe I need to address those feelings instead of taking them out on her. It's possible that my frustration is more about my own insecurities than her behavior. Another angle is the dynamic between us. If she's always talking about her job, maybe it's taking away from our time together. I might feel like she's not as present or that she's more focused on her work than our relationship. That could be another reason why her comments are bothering me. I should also think about how she reacted. She accused me of being jealous and suggested I work on my own issues. That might have made me feel defensive, leading to the argument. Maybe I should approach the conversation differently, focusing on how her comments make me feel instead of accusing her of bragging. In the end, I think both of us have valid points. She's proud of her job, and I can understand that. However, her constant talking about her perks might be coming off as bragging, especially in social settings where others might not have the same opportunities. I need to communicate my feelings without making her feel attacked, and she needs to be more aware of how her words affect others. So, am I the asshole? I think I might be partially. I should have handled the situation more gently, focusing on my feelings rather than accusing her of bragging. But she also needs to be more mindful of how her comments are perceived. It's a bit of both, but since I was the one who brought it up in a confrontational way, I might be more at fault.
